title.zh: 卷300 列傳八十七 沉起元 何师俭 唐继祖 马维翰 余甸 王葉滋 刘而位
title.en: Volume 300 Biographies 87: Chen Qi Yuan, He Shijian, Tang Jizu, Ma Weihan, Yu Dian, Wang Yezi, Liu Erwei
title.raw: 卷300 列傳八十七 沉起元 何师俭 唐继祖 马维翰 余甸 王葉滋 刘而位

sentences.zh: 列傳八十七

translations.literal: Biographies 87
translations.idiomatic: Biography 87

sentences.zh: 沈起元何師儉唐繼祖馬維翰餘甸王葉滋劉而位

translations.literal: Shen Qiyuan, He Shijian, Tang Jizu, Ma Weihan, Yu Dian, Wang Yezi, and Liu Erwei
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qiyuan, He Shijian, Tang Jizu, Ma Weihan, Yu Dian, Wang Yezi, and Liu Erwei

sentences.zh: 沈起元，字子大，江南太倉人。

translations.literal: Shen Qiyuan, courtesy name Zida, was a native of Taicang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qiyuan, styled Zida, came from Taicang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙六十年進士，選庶吉士，改吏部主事。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was transferred to be a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixtieth year of Kangxi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was then appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 擢員外郎，以知府發福建用。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director and was dispatched to Fujian to serve as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director, he was sent to Fujian to take up a prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 總督高其倬令權福州，調興化。

translations.literal: Governor-General Gao Qizhuo had him act as prefect of Fuzhou, then transferred him to Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Gao Qizhuo had him serve as acting prefect of Fuzhou before transferring him to Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 時世宗聞福建倉穀虧空，遣廣東巡撫楊文乾等往按，被劾者半，受代者爭為煩苛，起元獨持平。

translations.literal: At that time the Yongzheng Emperor heard that grain stores in Fujian were deficient; he sent Guangdong Governor Yang Wenqian and others to investigate. Half of those impeached were involved, and those replacing them vied to be harshly severe; Qiyuan alone remained fair and moderate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor learned that Fujian's granaries were short, he sent Guangdong Governor Yang Wenqian and others to investigate. Half of those implicated were punished, and their successors competed to be oppressively severe—only Qiyuan held a steady, even hand.

sentences.zh: 莆田民因訟互鬥，其倬恐釀亂，令捕治。

translations.literal: The people of Putian fought one another over lawsuits; Qizhuo feared this would breed disorder and ordered arrests.
translations.idiomatic: Litigants in Putian had come to blows; fearing unrest, Qizhuo ordered mass arrests.

sentences.zh: 起元責兩人而釋其餘，報曰：「罪在主者，餘不足問也。

translations.literal: Qiyuan held two men responsible and released the rest, reporting: "The guilt lies with the ringleaders; the others need not be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan punished only two ringleaders and released the rest, reporting: "The crime rests with the leaders; the others are not worth pursuing."

sentences.zh: 」尋攝海關，裁陋規萬餘金。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he took charge of the customs house and abolished improper fees amounting to more than ten thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took charge of the customs house as well and cut abusive levies worth more than ten thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 巡撫常安有奴在關，以索費困商舶。

translations.literal: Governor Chang An had a slave at the customs who extorted fees and harassed merchant vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chang An kept a servant at the customs gate who shook down merchant ships for fees.

sentences.zh: 起元聞，立督收稅如額，令商舶行，白常安斥奴。

translations.literal: When Qiyuan heard of this, he immediately supervised collection of taxes at the proper rate, let merchant ships proceed, and reported to Chang An to dismiss the slave.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of it, Qiyuan at once enforced the proper tax quota, cleared the ships to sail, and reported to Chang An to dismiss the servant.

sentences.zh: 自是人皆奉法。

translations.literal: From then on everyone obeyed the law.
translations.idiomatic: After that, everyone observed the regulations.

sentences.zh: 其倬奏開南洋，報可。

translations.literal: Qizhuo memorialized to open trade with the Southern Ocean, and approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhuo memorialized to reopen trade with Southeast Asia, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 已，復令商出洋者，必戚里具狀，限期返，逾者連坐。

translations.literal: Later, merchants going overseas were again required to have relatives provide bonds, with a fixed deadline for return; those who exceeded it would be punished by association.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward merchants sailing abroad were again required to obtain bonds from kinsmen, with a fixed date for return; failure would bring collective punishment on the family.

sentences.zh: 起元曰：「人之生死，貨之利鈍，皆無常，戚里豈能預料？

translations.literal: Qiyuan said: "Whether people live or die, whether goods profit or lose—all is uncertain; how can relatives possibly foresee this?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan said: "Life and death, profit and loss on the voyage—all are unpredictable. How can kinsmen possibly guarantee outcomes in advance?"

sentences.zh: 且始不聽出洋則已，今聽之，商造船集貨費不貲，奈何忽撓以結狀？

translations.literal: Moreover, if merchants were not allowed to go overseas at first, that would be one thing; now that they may go, they spend enormous sums building ships and assembling cargo—how can we suddenly disrupt them with bond requirements?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, if we had never allowed them to sail, that would be one matter; but now that permission is granted, merchants have sunk fortunes into building ships and gathering cargo—how can we suddenly disrupt them with bond formalities?

sentences.zh: 若令商自具狀，過三年不歸，勿聽回籍，不猶愈乎？

translations.literal: If merchants themselves provide bonds, and those who do not return within three years are barred from household registration, would that not be better?
translations.idiomatic: If merchants post their own bonds, and those who fail to return within three years forfeit their right to re-register at home—would that not be better?

sentences.zh: 」其倬從之。

translations.literal: Qizhuo followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhuo adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 調台灣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 台灣田一甲準十一畝有奇，賦三則：上則一甲穀八石，中則六石，下則四石，視內地數倍。

translations.literal: One jia of Taiwan farmland equals somewhat more than eleven mu; taxes are divided into three grades: the upper grade eight dan of grain per jia, the middle six dan, the lower four dan—several times those of the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiwan one jia of land equals a little over eleven mu; tax falls in three grades—eight dan of grain per jia at the upper rate, six at the middle, four at the lower—several times the levies on the mainland.

sentences.zh: 然多隱佔，民不甚困。

translations.literal: Yet much was concealed and occupied, so the people were not greatly burdened.
translations.idiomatic: Yet much land was concealed from the registers, so the people were not greatly burdened in practice.

sentences.zh: 時方清丈，佔者不得匿。

translations.literal: At that time a full land survey was underway, and occupiers could no longer hide.
translations.idiomatic: A comprehensive land survey was then under way, and concealed holdings could no longer be hidden.

sentences.zh: 其倬欲使台灣賦悉視內地下則，恐不及額致部詰。

translations.literal: Qizhuo wanted all Taiwan taxes set at the interior's lower grade, fearing failure to meet quotas would bring reproach from the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhuo wished to assess all Taiwan land at the mainland's lowest rate, fearing shortfalls would draw rebuke from the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 起元令著籍者仍舊額，丈出者視內地下則。

translations.literal: Qiyuan ordered registered land to keep the old quotas, while newly surveyed land to be taxed at the interior lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan ruled that land already on the registers should keep its old quota, while newly surveyed fields should be taxed at the mainland lower rate.

sentences.zh: 俟隱佔既清，更減舊額重者均於新額，賦不虧而民無累。

translations.literal: Once concealed occupation was cleared, heavier old quotas would be reduced and averaged into the new assessments—revenue would not fall short and the people would not be overburdened.
translations.idiomatic: Once concealed holdings were cleared, the heaviest old quotas could be reduced and spread across the new assessments—revenue would not fall short, and the people would not be crushed.

sentences.zh: 起元在福州，以辨冤獄忤按察使潘體豐，體豐中以他事，鐫四級，遂告歸。

translations.literal: While in Fuzhou, Qiyuan offended Judicial Commissioner Pan Tifeng by righting wrongful convictions; Tifeng framed him on other charges, demoted him four ranks, and he resigned to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In Fuzhou, Qiyuan offended Surveillance Commissioner Pan Tifeng by overturning unjust verdicts; Pan found a pretext to demote him four ranks, and he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，起江西驛鹽道副使。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended the throne, he was appointed vice commissioner of the Jiangxi Relay and Salt Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong came to the throne, Qiyuan was appointed vice commissioner of the Jiangxi Relay and Salt Circuit.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，擢河南按察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong he was promoted to Henan Judicial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianlong he was promoted to Henan surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會久雨，被災者四十餘縣，饑民四走，或議禁之。

translations.literal: Prolonged rain afflicted more than forty counties; starving people fled in all directions, and some proposed banning migration.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged rains had flooded more than forty counties; starving people scattered in every direction, and some officials proposed barring their movement.

sentences.zh: 起元謂：「民飢且死，奈何止其他徙？

translations.literal: Qiyuan said: "The people are starving and dying—how can we stop them from seeking relief elsewhere?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan said: "The people are starving to death—how can we forbid them to seek food elsewhere?"

sentences.zh: 」令安置未被水諸縣，給以糧，遂無出河南境者。

translations.literal: He ordered resettlement in counties not flooded and provided grain, so none left Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He had them settled in counties untouched by flood and issued grain rations, so none left the province.

sentences.zh: 巡撫雅爾圖檄府縣修書院，以起元總其事，乃教群士省身克己之學。

translations.literal: Governor Yarto ordered prefectures and counties to repair academies, with Qiyuan overseeing the work; he then taught scholars the discipline of self-examination and self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yarto ordered prefectures and counties to repair their academies and put Qiyuan in charge; he then instructed the scholars in the practice of moral self-scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 立章善坊，書孝子、悌弟、義夫、貞婦名，採訪事實，為章善錄版行，一時風動。

translations.literal: He established a "Exemplary Goodness" pavilion, inscribed the names of filial sons, respectful younger brothers, righteous husbands, and chaste wives, investigated the facts, and published a Record of Exemplary Goodness—morals stirred throughout the region.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a pavilion of exemplary virtue, inscribed the names of filial sons, dutiful younger brothers, righteous husbands, and chaste wives, verified each case, and published a Record of Exemplary Goodness that stirred public morals throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷直隸布政使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to be Financial Commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to financial commissioner of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 大旱議賑，總督高斌欲十一月始行，起元力請先普賑一月，俟戶口查竣，再分別加賑。

translations.literal: During a great drought relief was discussed; Governor-General Gao Bin wanted to begin in the eleventh month, but Qiyuan strongly urged universal relief for one month first, then differentiated additional relief after household registers were completed.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought, relief was debated; Governor-General Gao Bin wanted to wait until the eleventh month, but Qiyuan pressed for a month of universal relief first, then targeted additional aid once household registers were complete.

sentences.zh: 有倡言賑戶不賑口者，起元曰：「一戶數口，止賑一二，是且殺七八人矣！

translations.literal: Some advocated relief by household rather than by mouth; Qiyuan said: "A household has many members—if only one or two are fed, you will let seven or eight starve to death!"
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed relief by household rather than by individual; Qiyuan said: "A household may have many mouths—if you feed only one or two, you will let seven or eight starve!"

sentences.zh: 」檄各屬似此者罪之。

translations.literal: He ordered all subordinates to punish such practices.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all subordinates to punish officials who did likewise.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書海望奏清理直隸旗地，有司違限，旨飭責。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Haiwang memorialized to clear Zhili banner lands; local officials missed deadlines and were reprimanded by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Haiwang memorialized to clear banner lands in Zhili; local officials missed their deadlines and received an imperial reprimand.

sentences.zh: 斌將劾數州縣應命，起元不可，曰：「旗地非旦夕可清，州縣方賑災，何暇及此？

translations.literal: Bin was about to impeach several prefectures and counties to comply; Qiyuan objected: "Banner lands cannot be cleared overnight, and prefectures and counties are busy with famine relief—how can they attend to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Bin was about to impeach several prefectures and counties to force compliance; Qiyuan refused, saying: "Banner lands cannot be cleared overnight, and the counties are busy with famine relief—how can they attend to this now?"

sentences.zh: 獨劾起元可也！

translations.literal: Impeach me alone—that will do!"
translations.idiomatic: Impeach me alone—that will suffice!"

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: And so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 九年，內轉光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred within the capital to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred within the capital to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 十三年，移疾歸。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he cited illness and retired home.

sentences.zh: 起元自少敦厲廉恥，晚歲杜門誦先儒書。

translations.literal: From youth Qiyuan cultivated integrity and sense of shame; in his later years he shut his doors and recited the classics of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Qiyuan had cultivated integrity and a keen sense of shame; in his later years he shut his doors and devoted himself to the classics of the sages.

sentences.zh: 臨沒，言：「平生學無真得。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he said: "In life my learning gained no true attainment."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he said: "In life my learning never reached true understanding."

sentences.zh: 年來靜中自檢，仰不愧，俯不怍，或庶幾焉！

translations.literal: In recent years, examining myself in quiet, I look up without shame and down without guilt—perhaps that is something!"
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, examining myself in stillness, I can look up without shame and down without guilt—perhaps that is something!

sentences.zh: 何師儉，字桐叔，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: He Shijian, courtesy name Tongshu, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Shijian, styled Tongshu, came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 以納貲，於康熙六十年選授兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: By purchasing office, in the sixtieth year of Kangxi he was selected and appointed vice director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Having purchased office, in the sixtieth year of Kangxi he was selected and appointed a vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 奉職勤懇，常數月不出署。

translations.literal: He served diligently, often not leaving his yamen for months.
translations.idiomatic: He served with tireless diligence, often not leaving the yamen for months at a time.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，遷廣西右江道僉事，部請留任一年，世宗命以升銜留任，賜人葠、貂皮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was transferred to be commissioner of the Guangxi Right River Circuit; the ministry requested one year's retention; the Yongzheng Emperor ordered retention with promotion rank and bestowed ginseng and sable fur.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng he was transferred to the Guangxi Right River Circuit; the ministry asked that he be kept another year, and the Yongzheng Emperor ordered him retained with an elevated rank, bestowing ginseng and sable fur.

sentences.zh: 師儉以執法卻重賄，忤要人，因誣以避瘴故留部。

translations.literal: Shijian refused heavy bribes in enforcing the law, offended powerful men, and was falsely accused of staying in the capital to avoid malarial vapors.
translations.idiomatic: Shijian had refused heavy bribes while enforcing the law, offending powerful figures, who then slandered him as staying in the capital to avoid the southern miasma.

sentences.zh: 侍郎李紱昌言曰：「今部曹不名一錢，才者尤勞瘁，苟得郡，爭趨之，況監司耶？

translations.literal: Vice Minister Li Fu spoke openly: "Nowadays ministry officers won't take a single coin; the capable are especially worn out—if they could get a prefecture they would rush for it, let alone a circuit intendant?"
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Li Fu spoke plainly: "Nowadays ministry officers won't touch a single coin; the ablest are worn to exhaustion—if they could secure a prefecture they would rush for it at once, let alone a circuit post?"

sentences.zh: 」期滿，復請留，加按察司副使銜。

translations.literal: When the term expired he again requested retention, with vice commissioner of surveillance rank added.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he again asked to stay, and was given the rank of vice surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 司疏奏皆出其手，他司事難治者亦時委之。

translations.literal: All ministry memorials were drafted by his hand; difficult matters from other bureaus were also entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: All ministry memorials passed through his hand, and difficult cases from other bureaus were often entrusted to him as well.

sentences.zh: 三年，出為江南驛鹽道副使，上召對，勉以操守，复賜人葠、貂皮，許上疏言事。

translations.literal: In the third year he went out as Jiangnan Relay and Salt vice commissioner; the emperor summoned him for audience, exhorted integrity, again bestowed ginseng and sable, and permitted memorials on any matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was posted as Jiangnan Relay and Salt vice commissioner; the emperor received him in audience, urged him to maintain his integrity, again bestowed ginseng and sable fur, and allowed him to submit memorials on any matter.

sentences.zh: 四年，調廣東糧驛道副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Guangdong Grain and Relay vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Guangdong Grain and Relay vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歲大祲，師儉以存留米五萬石給餉，飭所屬緩徵。

translations.literal: A great famine struck; Shijian used fifty thousand shi of retained grain for provisions and ordered subordinates to defer collection.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought severe famine; Shijian drew on fifty thousand shi of retained grain for rations and ordered his subordinates to defer tax collection.

sentences.zh: 或疑專擅獲咎，師儉曰：「請而後行，民已苦箠楚矣！

translations.literal: Some feared unauthorized action would bring blame; Shijian said: "If we wait for approval before acting, the people will already suffer the lash!"
translations.idiomatic: Some worried he would be punished for acting on his own authority; Shijian said: "If we wait for approval before acting, the people will already have felt the rod!"

sentences.zh: 」總督孔毓珣與巡撫楊文乾不相能，以師儉署鹽法道，欲引以為助。

translations.literal: Governor-General Kong Yupei and Governor Yang Wenqian were at odds; Kong had Shijian act as Salt Commissioner to win his support.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Kong Yupei and Governor Yang Wenqian were at odds; Kong had Shijian act as salt commissioner, hoping to win his support.

sentences.zh: 文乾疑為毓珣黨，令買銅，將以賠累困之。

translations.literal: Wenqian suspected he was Kong's ally and ordered him to buy copper, intending to entangle him in losses.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian suspected him of being Kong's man and ordered him to purchase copper, intending to ruin him through indemnity losses.

sentences.zh: 明年，文乾入覲，上示以毓珣彈事，亦及師儉，乃知師儉非阿毓珣者。

translations.literal: The next year Wenqian came to court; the emperor showed him Kong's impeachment memorials, including Shijian's, and learned Shijian did not favor Kong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wenqian came to court; the emperor showed him Kong's impeachment memorials, which also mentioned Shijian, and realized Shijian was no partisan of Kong's.

sentences.zh: 令署按察使，毓珣又疑師儉暱文乾。

translations.literal: He was ordered to act as surveillance commissioner; Kong then suspected Shijian was close to Wenqian.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to act as surveillance commissioner, whereupon Kong suspected Shijian of being close to Wenqian.

sentences.zh: 及文乾卒，劾師儉違禁開礦，侵蝕銅價。

translations.literal: When Wenqian died, Kong impeached Shijian for illegally opening mines and embezzling copper funds.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenqian died, Kong impeached Shijian for illegally opening mines and embezzling copper revenues.

sentences.zh: 逾年，署巡撫傅泰會鞫，事始白。

translations.literal: A year later Acting Governor Fu Tai jointly investigated and the matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, Acting Governor Fu Tai jointly investigated the case and Shijian was exonerated.

sentences.zh: 上知其無罪，命往陝西佐治軍需。

translations.literal: The emperor knew him innocent and ordered him to Shaanxi to assist with military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew him innocent and ordered him to Shaanxi to assist with military logistics.

sentences.zh: 師儉在兵部，諳悉諸邊形勢扼塞、戰守機宜、芻餉緩急。

translations.literal: At the War Ministry Shijian was thoroughly versed in border terrain chokepoints, offensive and defensive tactics, and the urgency of fodder and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: At the War Ministry Shijian had mastered the strategic terrain of every frontier, the tactics of attack and defense, and the urgency of fodder and supply.

sentences.zh: 至涼州，每集議，指畫如素習，總督查郎阿深重之。

translations.literal: At Liangzhou, at every council he directed affairs as if long practiced; Governor-General Zha Lang'a valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: At Liangzhou, at every council he laid out plans as though he had long practiced the art; Governor-General Zha Lang'a held him in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 署涼莊道參政。

translations.literal: He acted as Liangzhuang Circuit administrative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting administrative commissioner of the Liangzhuang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 師過涼州，檄至肅州支餉。

translations.literal: When the army passed Liangzhou, orders came to supply provisions at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the army passed through Liangzhou, orders arrived to provision them at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 兩路遙遠，師儉即以涼州所蓄給之，師行無乏。

translations.literal: Both routes were remote; Shijian supplied from Liangzhou stores, and the army marched without want.
translations.idiomatic: Both routes were distant; Shijian supplied the troops from Liangzhou's stores, and the army marched without shortage.

sentences.zh: 一日羽書數過，師儉策必調取生兵，峙餦以待。

translations.literal: One day urgent dispatches arrived repeatedly; Shijian surmised fresh troops would be called and prepared rations in advance.
translations.idiomatic: One day urgent dispatches arrived in quick succession; Shijian surmised that fresh troops would be called up and prepared rations in advance.

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: And so it proved.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 肅州師將行，飛檄令截取公私騾馬，官民皇皇。

translations.literal: At Suzhou, as the army was to march, flying orders came to seize all private and official mules; officials and people were in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: At Suzhou, as the army was about to march, urgent orders came to seize all private and official mules and horses, throwing officials and commoners into panic.

sentences.zh: 師儉曰：「在道官商皆赴肅者，若官頓於途，貨棄於地，非軍前所宜。

translations.literal: Shijian said: "Officials and merchants on the road are all heading to Suzhou—if officials halt en route and goods are abandoned, that is unsuitable for the front."
translations.idiomatic: Shijian said: "Officials and merchants on the road are all bound for Suzhou—if we halt them en route and goods are abandoned along the way, that will not serve the army."

sentences.zh: 進剿未有定期，何如聽其至肅，釋所載而後供役？

translations.literal: The advance has no fixed date—why not let them reach Suzhou, unload, then provide service?
translations.idiomatic: The campaign has no fixed date—why not let them reach Suzhou, unload their goods, and then provide transport?

sentences.zh: 軍前得人與貨，亦省芻茭解送之煩，是獲兩利也。

translations.literal: The front gains men and goods while saving the trouble of hauling fodder—both sides profit.
translations.idiomatic: The front gains both manpower and goods while sparing the trouble of hauling fodder over long distances—both sides benefit.

sentences.zh: 檄雖嚴，吾自當之。

translations.literal: Though the order is strict, I will bear responsibility myself.
translations.idiomatic: Though the order is strict, I will bear the responsibility myself.

sentences.zh: 」於是官商皆安，軍事亦無誤。

translations.literal: Officials and merchants were reassured and military affairs proceeded without mishap.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and merchants were reassured, and military operations proceeded without disruption.

sentences.zh: 尋調補西安鹽驛道副使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to fill the Xi'an Salt and Relay vice commissioner post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to fill the post of Xi'an Salt and Relay vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 關中旱，詔以湖廣米十萬石自商州龍駒寨運陝西。

translations.literal: Guanzhong suffered drought; an edict ordered one hundred thousand shi of Huguang grain transported from Shangzhou Longjuzhai to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong was stricken by drought; an edict ordered one hundred thousand shi of Huguang grain transported from Shangzhou's Longjuzhai to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 師儉董其役，未半，大雨谿漲，騾馬少，不足供轉輸。

translations.literal: Shijian directed the task; halfway through heavy rain swelled streams, mules were few, and transport fell short.
translations.idiomatic: Shijian directed the transport; before it was half done, heavy rains swelled the streams, mules were scarce, and delivery fell short.

sentences.zh: 商於山中無頓積所，水次隘，運艘不齊。

translations.literal: In the Shangyu mountains there were no storage depots; river landings were narrow and transport boats did not arrive together.
translations.idiomatic: In the mountains of Shangyu there were no depots for stockpiling; river landings were cramped and transport boats did not arrive together.

sentences.zh: 師儉以秋穀將登，請止運，民亦不飢。

translations.literal: Shijian noted autumn grain would soon ripen and requested stopping transport—the people would not starve.
translations.idiomatic: Shijian noted that the autumn harvest was near and requested that transport be halted—the people would not go hungry.

sentences.zh: 軍中馬缺，檄取驛馬。

translations.literal: The army lacked horses; orders came to take relay horses.
translations.idiomatic: The army was short of horses; orders came to requisition relay horses.

sentences.zh: 師儉謂：「置郵傳命，如人身血脈，不能一日廢。

translations.literal: Shijian said: "The postal relay system is like the blood vessels of the body—it cannot be suspended for a day."
translations.idiomatic: Shijian said: "The postal relay system is like the blood vessels of the body—it cannot be suspended for a single day."

sentences.zh: 」拒不可，事竟寢。

translations.literal: He refused; the matter was finally dropped.
translations.idiomatic: He refused; the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 擢按察使，數平疑獄。

translations.literal: Promoted to surveillance commissioner, he repeatedly resolved doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to surveillance commissioner, he repeatedly resolved doubtful cases.

sentences.zh: 吏有故入人罪者，必按如法，雖貴勢賢親不徇縱。

translations.literal: Officials who falsely implicated others were punished by law; even the powerful and well-connected were not indulged.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who falsely implicated others were punished according to law; even the powerful and well-connected were not spared.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以目疾乞休。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he requested retirement due to eye disease.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he requested retirement on account of eye disease.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，赦詔至，時目已失明，令吏誦案牘，諦聽，得邀赦典者，立出之而後上陳。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended and amnesty arrived, he was already blind; he had clerks read case documents, listened carefully, immediately released those qualifying for amnesty, then reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended the throne and the amnesty edict arrived, he was already blind; he had clerks read out the case documents, listened intently, immediately released those eligible for amnesty, and only then reported upward.

sentences.zh: 留兩月，畢其事始歸。

translations.literal: He stayed two months until all matters were finished before returning home.
translations.idiomatic: He remained two months until all matters were concluded before returning home.

sentences.zh: 後卒於家，陝西祀名宦。

translations.literal: He later died at home and was enshrined among celebrated officials in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at home and was enshrined among celebrated local officials in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 唐繼祖，字序皇，江南江都人。

translations.literal: Tang Jizu, courtesy name Xuhuang, was a native of Jiangdu in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jizu, styled Xuhuang, came from Jiangdu in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙六十年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year of Kangxi he became a jinshi and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixtieth year of Kangxi and entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，散館，授編修，轉禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he left the Hanlin academy, was appointed compiler, and transferred to be vice director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng he completed his Hanlin term, was appointed a compiler, and transferred to a vice directorship in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五年，考選浙江道御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was examined and selected as censor of the Zhejiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was examined and selected as censor of the Zhejiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 七年，授工科給事中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 命察八旗虧帑，律侵挪皆不赦，犯者貧，羈獄二三十年不結。

translations.literal: He was ordered to investigate Eight Banner treasury deficits; the law held that embezzlement was unforgivable; offenders were poor and languished in prison twenty or thirty years unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to investigate deficits in the Eight Banners' treasuries; the law held that embezzlement was unpardonable, yet offenders were often destitute and languished in prison twenty or thirty years without resolution.

sentences.zh: 繼祖為核減開除，奏請豁免，積牘一清。

translations.literal: Jizu verified reductions and dismissals, memorialized for exemptions, and cleared the accumulated backlog of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu audited the reductions and dismissals, memorialized for exemptions, and cleared the backlog of cases entirely.

sentences.zh: 命巡西城，回民聚居，頑獷不法，嚴治之，有犯必懲，悉斂戢。

translations.literal: He was ordered to patrol the western city; Hui people lived there in concentration, obstinate and lawless; he governed them strictly, punishing every offense, and all were subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to patrol the western quarter, where Hui communities were concentrated and notoriously unruly, he enforced the law strictly, punishing every offense until all were brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 建倉東便門外，多發塚墓，毀祠宇，繼祖陳其不便，改地營建，塚墓祠宇並修復。

translations.literal: A granary was to be built outside the East Convenient Gate, requiring many graves to be opened and shrines destroyed; Jizu memorialized on the inconvenience, the site was changed, and graves and shrines were all restored.
translations.idiomatic: Plans to build a granary outside the East Convenient Gate would have opened many graves and destroyed shrines; Jizu memorialized against it, the site was moved, and the graves and shrines were restored.

sentences.zh: 南漕愆期，命赴淮安巡視。

translations.literal: Southern tribute grain was overdue; he was ordered to go to Huai'an to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: When southern tribute grain fell behind schedule, he was ordered to Huai'an to oversee transport.

sentences.zh: 繼祖馳至，不更張成法，惟選幹吏催督，懲其疲惰。

translations.literal: Jizu hurried there, did not alter established regulations, but only selected capable officials to urge supervision and punished the slack.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu hurried there without changing established procedures, but selected capable officers to press the work forward and punished the negligent.

sentences.zh: 兩閱月，糧艘悉抵通州。

translations.literal: Within two months all grain transports reached Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within two months every grain transport had reached Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 條上漕務利病，下部議行。

translations.literal: He submitted detailed points on the benefits and harms of grain transport affairs; the ministry deliberated and implemented them.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a detailed memorial on the strengths and weaknesses of the grain transport system, which the ministry adopted.

sentences.zh: 七年，命往湖南讞獄，並巡察湖南、湖北兩省，裹糧出，有餽觴酒豆肉，皆卻之，令行禁止。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to Hunan to judge cases and inspect both Hunan and Hubei; he traveled with his own provisions, refused all gifts of wine, meat, or food, and issued orders forbidding such practices.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was sent to Hunan to adjudicate cases and inspect both Hunan and Hubei; he traveled on his own provisions, refused every gift of food or drink, and issued orders banning such practices.

sentences.zh: 與巡撫趙申喬同按永順苗變獄，群情帖服，苗疆以安。

translations.literal: Together with Governor Zhao Shenqiao he jointly investigated the Yongshun Miao rebellion case; public sentiment was satisfied and the Miao frontier was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Governor Zhao Shenqiao he investigated the Yongshun Miao uprising; the people were satisfied and the Miao frontier was pacified.

sentences.zh: 湖南捕役多通盜，奏請捕役為盜，加重治罪，報可，入新例。

translations.literal: Hunan constables often colluded with bandits; he memorialized that constables who became bandits should receive heavier punishment; approval was granted and it entered the new statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan constables often colluded with bandits; he memorialized that constables who turned bandit should face heavier penalties; the court approved, and it entered the new code.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢通政司參議。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢鴻臚寺卿。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 尋命以本銜署河南按察使，旋授湖北按察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to act as Henan surveillance commissioner at his current rank, then appointed Hubei surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to act as Henan surveillance commissioner at his current rank, then appointed surveillance commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 繼祖在兩湖久，熟知吏民情偽。

translations.literal: Jizu had long been in the two Hu regions and thoroughly knew the truth and falsehood of officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Having long served in the two Hu provinces, Jizu knew the officials and people through and through.

sentences.zh: 楚俗刁健，黠吏與姦豪通，伺官喜怒，訟益難治。

translations.literal: Chu customs were contentious and sharp; cunning clerks colluded with powerful scoundrels, watching officials' moods, and lawsuits grew harder to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei folk were litigious and sharp; cunning clerks colluded with local strongmen, watching officials' moods, and lawsuits grew ever harder to settle.

sentences.zh: 繼祖閉諸胥於一室，不令與外通，訟風衰減。

translations.literal: Jizu confined all clerks in one room, forbidding contact with outsiders, and the litigation craze diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu confined all clerks in one room, cut off their outside contacts, and the culture of litigation subsided.

sentences.zh: 雪監利女子冤獄，按鍾祥民變，皆為時所稱。

translations.literal: He cleared a wrongful conviction of a woman in Jianli and investigated the Zhongxiang popular disturbance—both were praised in their time.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared a wrongful conviction of a woman in Jianli and investigated the popular disturbance at Zhongxiang—both won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 世宗馭吏嚴，內外大僚凜凜，救過不暇。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor governed officials strictly; high officials within and without were in awe, too busy covering faults to spare.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor ruled officials with iron discipline; high officers inside and outside the capital lived in dread, scrambling merely to cover their mistakes.

sentences.zh: 繼祖一意展舒，所陳奏無不允。

translations.literal: Jizu alone acted with ease and openness; every memorial he submitted was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu alone acted with confidence and ease; every memorial he submitted won approval.

sentences.zh: 上欲大用之，出巡察，賜以摺匣，許奏事，曰：「朕於督撫賢者始賜摺匣，汝宜好為之！

translations.literal: The emperor wished to employ him greatly; on going out to inspect, he was bestowed a memorial folder and permitted to report affairs, saying: "I bestow the memorial folder only on worthy governors and governors-general—you should do well with it!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor intended to promote him further; when he went out on inspection he was given a memorial folder and permission to report directly, saying: "I grant the memorial folder only to worthy governors—you must make good use of it!"

sentences.zh: 」調江西，未之任，以疾乞歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangxi but did not take up the post, citing illness to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jiangxi but never took up the post, citing illness to return home.

sentences.zh: 病癒將出，遽卒。

translations.literal: When his illness healed and he was about to depart, he suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he recovered and was preparing to leave, he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 馬維翰，字墨麟，浙江海鹽人。

translations.literal: Ma Weihan, courtesy name Molin, was a native of Haiyan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Weihan, styled Molin, came from Haiyan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙六十年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the sixtieth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixtieth year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，授吏部主事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng he was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 甫視事，杖姦胥，銓政清肅。

translations.literal: As soon as he took office he flogged corrupt clerks, and personnel administration became clear and strict.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took office he had corrupt clerks beaten, and personnel administration became scrupulously clean.

sentences.zh: 轉員外郎，考選陝西道御史，遷工科給事中，監督倉場，所至有聲。

translations.literal: Transferred to vice director, examined and selected as censor of the Shaanxi Circuit, promoted to supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works, supervised the granaries, and wherever he went gained reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director, then examined and selected as Shaanxi Circuit censor, then supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works supervising the granaries—wherever he served he won renown.

sentences.zh: 六年，命赴四川清丈田畝，時同奉使者四。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to Sichuan to survey land; at that time four commissioners were sent on the same mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was ordered to Sichuan to conduct a land survey; four commissioners were sent on the mission together.

sentences.zh: 維翰分赴建昌道屬，具有條理，糧浮於田者必請減，逾年事竣。

translations.literal: Weihan went to the Jianchang Circuit jurisdiction, worked with clear method, always requested reduction where grain tax exceeded land, and finished within a year.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan took charge of the Jianchang Circuit jurisdiction, worked methodically, always sought reductions where tax exceeded registered land, and finished within a year.

sentences.zh: 御史吳濤在川東丈田不實，以維翰助之。

translations.literal: Censor Wu Tao surveyed land in eastern Sichuan dishonestly and implicated Weihan as his accomplice.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wu Tao had falsified the land survey in eastern Sichuan and tried to implicate Weihan as his accomplice.

sentences.zh: 至則發其弊，遂以維翰代任。

translations.literal: When Weihan arrived he exposed the fraud, and Weihan was put in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Weihan arrived he exposed the fraud, and was appointed to take over Wu's duties.

sentences.zh: 巡撫憲德薦可大用。

translations.literal: Governor Xiande recommended him for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xiande recommended him for higher appointment.

sentences.zh: 八年，留補建昌道副使，疏陳二事：四川俗好訟，州縣斷獄苟簡，案牘不具，奸民輒翻控，淆亂是非，請設幕職以襄治理；

translations.literal: In the eighth year he remained to fill the Jianchang Circuit vice commissioner post and memorialized on two matters: Sichuan customs favored litigation; prefectures and counties judged cases carelessly with incomplete records, and scoundrels repeatedly appealed to confuse right and wrong—he requested staff posts to assist governance;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was retained as Jianchang Circuit vice commissioner and memorialized on two matters: Sichuan was litigious; prefectures and counties judged cases carelessly with incomplete records, allowing scoundrels to appeal repeatedly and confuse right and wrong—he proposed establishing staff posts to assist governance;

sentences.zh: 又民鮮土著，多結草屋，輕於遷徙，焚劫輒致災，請發官款造磚甓，勸民多建瓦屋。

translations.literal: Moreover the people were rarely settled natives, mostly building thatched huts and moving lightly—fire and robbery often brought disaster—he requested official funds to make bricks and tiles and urge the people to build more tile-roofed houses.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover few people were long-settled natives; most lived in thatched huts and moved readily—fires and raids brought frequent disaster—he proposed official funds to manufacture bricks and tiles and encourage the people to build tile-roofed houses.

sentences.zh: 上斥其非政要，以其疏示憲德，謂：「汝薦可大用者乃若此！

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked these as not essential to governance, showed the memorial to Xiande, and said: "The man you recommended for great employment is like this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed these as peripheral to governance, showed the memorial to Xiande, and said: "This is the man you recommended for great things!"

sentences.zh: 」然維翰勇於任事，相度要害，改黎州千戶所設清溪縣。

translations.literal: Yet Weihan was bold in undertaking affairs, surveyed strategic points, and changed the Lizhou guard post into Qingxi County.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Weihan was bold in action; surveying strategic points, he converted the Lizhou guard post into Qingxi County.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙苗亂，出師會剿，維翰治軍需，供糗糧芻茭，鑿雪通道，與廝卒同甘苦。

translations.literal: When the Wumeng Miao rebelled, troops were sent for joint suppression; Weihan managed military supplies, provided rations and fodder, cut paths through snow, and shared hardship with common soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wumeng Miao rebelled and troops were dispatched, Weihan managed military logistics, supplied rations and fodder, cut paths through snow, and shared hardship with the rank and file.

sentences.zh: 論剿撫悉中機宜，事乃定。

translations.literal: His arguments on suppression and pacification all hit the mark, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel on suppression and pacification proved sound, and the affair was settled.

sentences.zh: 涼山地震數百里，勘災散賑，民感之。

translations.literal: An earthquake in Liangshan shook hundreds of li; he surveyed the disaster and distributed relief, and the people were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: An earthquake in Liangshan devastated hundreds of li; he surveyed the damage and distributed relief, winning the people's gratitude.

sentences.zh: 礦廠擾蠻，起為亂，方進剿。

translations.literal: Mining operations disturbed the tribes, who rose in rebellion, and suppression was underway.
translations.idiomatic: Mining operations provoked the tribes into rebellion, and a punitive campaign was under way.

sentences.zh: 維翰力陳營兵不戢及各廠病蠻狀，請罷廠撤兵，撫各番，止誅其魁。

translations.literal: Weihan strongly memorialized on undisciplined camp soldiers and the suffering of tribes at each mine, requesting closure of mines, withdrawal of troops, pacification of each tribe, and execution of only the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan strongly memorialized on undisciplined soldiers and the tribes' suffering at each mine, urging closure of the mines, withdrawal of troops, pacification of each tribe, and punishment of only the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 在川七年，不阿上官。

translations.literal: Seven years in Sichuan, he never curried favor with superiors.
translations.idiomatic: During seven years in Sichuan he never curried favor with his superiors.

sentences.zh: 旋被構，維翰揭部請解職赴質。

translations.literal: Soon he was framed; Weihan petitioned the ministry to resign and come to answer charges.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon framed; Weihan petitioned the ministry to resign his post and come to the capital to answer the charges.

sentences.zh: 時親王總部事，特威重，捽使免冠。

translations.literal: At that time a prince oversaw ministry affairs with special authority and dignity, and had him seized and stripped of his cap.
translations.idiomatic: A prince then oversaw ministry affairs with exceptional authority and had him seized and stripped of his official cap.

sentences.zh: 維翰以手按冠抗聲曰：「奉旨不免冠！

translations.literal: Weihan held his cap with his hand and protested loudly: "By imperial decree one need not remove the cap!"
translations.idiomatic: Weihan held his cap in place and protested loudly: "By imperial decree I am not required to remove my cap!"

sentences.zh: 」譙問故，則又抗聲曰：「旨解職，非革職也！

translations.literal: When rebuked and asked why, he again protested loudly: "The decree was to resign office, not to be dismissed from office!"
translations.idiomatic: When rebuked and asked why, he protested again: "The decree was to resign my post, not to strip me of rank!"

sentences.zh: 」部乃疏請奪官。

translations.literal: The ministry then memorialized requesting deprivation of office.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry then memorialized to strip him of his rank.

sentences.zh: 事旋白。

translations.literal: The matter was soon cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was soon cleared.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，起授江南常鎮道參議。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong he was recalled and appointed administrative commissioner of the Jiangnan Changzhen Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianlong he was recalled and appointed administrative commissioner of the Jiangnan Changzhen Circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he returned home and died there.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he returned home and died there.

sentences.zh: 餘甸，字田生，福建福清人。

translations.literal: Yu Dian, courtesy name Tiansheng, was a native of Fuqing in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dian, styled Tiansheng, came from Fuqing in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the forty-fifth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-fifth year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 居鄉勵名節，巡撫張伯行重之，延主鼇峰書院。

translations.literal: While at home he cultivated reputation and integrity; Governor Zhang Boxing valued him and invited him to head the Aofeng Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At home he cultivated reputation and integrity; Governor Zhang Boxing esteemed him and invited him to head the Aofeng Academy.

sentences.zh: 授四川江津知縣，民投牒者，片言立決遣，訟為之簡。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Jiangjin in Sichuan, he decided petitions in a few words and dismissed them at once, and litigation was thereby simplified.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Jiangjin in Sichuan, he settled petitions in a few words and dismissed them at once, greatly reducing litigation.

sentences.zh: 日與諸生誦說文藝，疏解性理。

translations.literal: Daily he lectured students on literary arts and explained moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he lectured students on literature and expounded moral philosophy.

sentences.zh: 所徵賦即儲庫，不入私室。

translations.literal: Taxes collected were stored directly in the treasury, never entering his private quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes collected went straight to the public treasury, never into his private quarters.

sentences.zh: 時青海用兵，巡撫年羹堯督餉，多額外急徵，檄再三至，甸不應。

translations.literal: At that time Qinghai was at war; Governor Nian Gengyao supervised supplies and imposed many extra urgent levies; orders came repeatedly but Dian did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghai was then at war; Governor Nian Gengyao supervised supplies and imposed many extra urgent levies—orders arrived repeatedly, but Dian refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 乃使僕持檄告諭，自朝至晡，甸不出，使者譁。

translations.literal: Nian then sent a servant bearing orders to announce; from morning to evening Dian did not come out, and the messenger clamored.
translations.idiomatic: Nian then sent a servant with orders; from morning until evening Dian did not emerge, and the messenger raised an uproar.

sentences.zh: 甸坐堂皇，命反接，將杖之，丞簿力為請，久之乃釋其縛。

translations.literal: Dian sat in the main hall, ordered him bound hand behind back and was about to beat him; the assistants pleaded earnestly, and only after long delay were his bonds released.
translations.idiomatic: Dian sat in the main hall, ordered the messenger bound and was about to have him beaten; his deputies pleaded earnestly, and only after a long delay were the bonds removed.

sentences.zh: 越日，使者索檄，甸曰：「汝還報，我閉門待劾，檄已達京師矣。

translations.literal: The next day the messenger demanded the order; Dian said: "Go back and report—I shut my doors awaiting impeachment; the order has already reached the capital."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the messenger demanded the order back; Dian said: "Go report that I have shut my doors awaiting impeachment—the order has already reached the capital."

sentences.zh: 」羹堯亦置之。

translations.literal: Gengyao also let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao let the matter drop as well.

sentences.zh: 行取吏部主事，時尚書張鵬翮、侍郎湯右曾皆以幹濟名，甸遇當爭辯者，侃侃無所撓。

translations.literal: Selected for promotion to principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel; at that time Minister Zhang Penghe and Vice Minister Tang Youzeng were both famed for capability; when matters required debate Dian spoke forthrightly without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for the Ministry of Personnel as principal secretary; Minister Zhang Penghe and Vice Minister Tang Youzeng were both famed for capability—when debate was needed, Dian spoke forthrightly and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 主選三年，權要富人請託多格不行。

translations.literal: He oversaw appointments for three years; requests from the powerful and wealthy were mostly rejected.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw appointments for three years, rejecting most requests from the powerful and wealthy.

sentences.zh: 將告歸，條文書已駁議未奏者十餘事，曰：「此皆作姦巧法易為所蒙，必上聞，吾乃去。

translations.literal: About to request retirement, he listed more than ten documents already rejected in deliberation but not yet memorialized, saying: "These all devise crafty methods easily used to deceive— they must be reported upward before I leave."
translations.idiomatic: About to retire, he listed more than ten documents already rejected in deliberation but not yet submitted, saying: "These devise crafty loopholes easily exploited—I must report them before I leave."

sentences.zh: 」父憂免喪，猶廬墓。

translations.literal: After mourning for his father ended, he still dwelt by the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he still kept vigil at his father's tomb.

sentences.zh: 以河道總督陳鵬年疏薦，擢山東兗寧道。

translations.literal: On recommendation by Grand Canal Governor Chen Pengnian he was promoted to the Shandong Yanning Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On Grand Canal Governor Chen Pengnian's recommendation he was promoted to the Shandong Yanning Circuit.

sentences.zh: 釐工剔弊，一袪積習，甚得士民心。

translations.literal: He regulated works and eliminated abuses, sweeping away entrenched customs, and won the hearts of scholars and common people.
translations.idiomatic: He regulated public works and eliminated abuses, sweeping away entrenched customs and winning the hearts of gentry and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 鵬年卒，齊蘇勒為河督，以工事劾甸，行河至濟寧，士民群聚乞還甸。

translations.literal: When Pengnian died, Qisuole became canal governor and impeached Dian over engineering works; traveling the canal to Jining, scholars and people gathered begging for Dian's return.
translations.idiomatic: When Pengnian died, Qisuole became canal governor and impeached Dian over engineering works; as he traveled the canal to Jining, scholars and commoners gathered begging for Dian's return.

sentences.zh: 齊蘇勒疏陳，召入見。

translations.literal: Qisuole memorialized on the matter, and Dian was summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Qisuole memorialized on the matter, and Dian was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年四月，授山東按察使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yongzheng he was appointed Shandong surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Yongzheng he was appointed Shandong surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 攜二僕，買驢之官，務崇禮教，輕刑罰，政化大行。

translations.literal: He took two servants, bought a donkey to go to office, devoted himself to promoting ritual teaching, lightened punishments, and civilizing influence spread widely.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled with two servants on a donkey he had bought, promoted ritual education, lightened punishments, and his civilizing influence spread widely.

sentences.zh: 十一月，召詣京師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢順天府丞。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to vice director of the Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to vice director of the Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甸歷官盡革陋規，為按察使，愍囚不能自衣食，取鹽商歲饋三之一以資給之。

translations.literal: Throughout his offices Dian abolished improper customs; as surveillance commissioner, pitying prisoners unable to feed and clothe themselves, he took one-third of the salt merchants' annual gifts to support them.
translations.idiomatic: In every post Dian abolished abusive customs; as surveillance commissioner, pitying prisoners who could not feed themselves, he took one-third of the salt merchants' annual gifts to support them.

sentences.zh: 兼完囹圄，修學宮、書院，委有司出入註籍。

translations.literal: He also repaired prisons, restored the Confucian temple and academy, and entrusted officials to register all comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: He also repaired the prisons, restored the Confucian temple and academy, and had officials register all entries and exits.

sentences.zh: 既去官，上命內閣學士繆沅清察山東鹽政諸弊，舉是劾甸，奪官，歸。

translations.literal: After he left office the emperor ordered Grand Secretariat academician Miu Yuan to investigate abuses in Shandong salt administration; citing this, Dian was impeached, deprived of office, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After he left office the emperor ordered Grand Secretariat academician Miu Yuan to investigate Shandong salt administration; citing this matter, Dian was impeached, stripped of rank, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 甸用唐人詩語為人書楹帖，其人有怨家，訐於有司，以為怨望。

translations.literal: Dian wrote couplets for someone using Tang poetry; the man had an enemy who reported to officials that it expressed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Dian had written couplets for someone using lines from Tang poetry; the man's enemy reported to officials that the verses expressed disloyal resentment.

sentences.zh: 有司以甸所書也，並下甸於獄。

translations.literal: Because Dian had written them, officials imprisoned Dian as well.
translations.idiomatic: Because Dian had written the couplets, officials imprisoned him as well.

sentences.zh: 事白，遽卒。

translations.literal: When the matter was cleared, he suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was cleared, he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 王葉滋，字槐青，江南華亭人。

translations.literal: Wang Yezi, courtesy name Huaiqing, was a native of Huating in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yezi, styled Huaiqing, came from Huating in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，補諸生。

translations.literal: In his early twenties he became a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he became a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫硃軾闢佐幕，器其才。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor Zhu Shi invited him as staff aide and valued his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Governor Zhu Shi invited him into his staff and valued his talent.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，重開明史館，軾薦之，引見稱旨，命入館纂修。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng the Ming History Office was reopened; Shi recommended him; audience pleased the emperor, and he was ordered to enter the office to compile.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng the Ming History Office reopened; Zhu recommended him; the emperor received him favorably and ordered him to join the compilation staff.

sentences.zh: 舉順天鄉試。

translations.literal: He passed the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Shuntian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 福敏督湖廣，世宗命葉滋往贊其幕。

translations.literal: Fu Min supervised Huguang; the Yongzheng Emperor ordered Yezi to assist his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Min was appointed governor-general of Huguang; the Yongzheng Emperor ordered Yezi to assist his staff.

sentences.zh: 五年，應禮部試，甫畢，上召見，問湖廣吏治、民生利弊，奏對甚悉，趣馳傳還湖廣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he took the Ministry of Rites examination; as soon as it ended the emperor summoned him, asked about Huguang administration and people's welfare, and he answered in full detail; he was urged to return swiftly to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he took the Ministry of Rites examination; as soon as it ended the emperor summoned him, questioned him on Huguang administration and the people's welfare, and he answered in thorough detail; the emperor urged him to return swiftly to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 榜發中式，未與殿試，賜二甲進士，即授常德知府。

translations.literal: When the list was published he had passed; without taking the palace examination he was granted second-rank jinshi and immediately appointed prefect of Changde.
translations.idiomatic: When the results were published he had passed; without taking the palace examination he was granted second-rank jinshi and immediately appointed prefect of Changde.

sentences.zh: 常德例，知府至，行戶更新照，規費四千金，葉滋革其例。

translations.literal: By Changde custom, when a prefect arrived, merchant guilds renewed their licenses at a fee of four thousand taels; Yezi abolished this custom.
translations.idiomatic: By Changde custom, when a new prefect arrived the merchant guilds paid four thousand taels to renew their licenses; Yezi abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 境數被水災，請帑增築花貓新陂堤堰，豁被水荒田額糧，民德之。

translations.literal: The district had often suffered floods; he requested funds to enlarge the Huamao and Xinpi dikes, and remitted grain tax on flooded wasteland; the people were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: The district had suffered repeated floods; he requested funds to enlarge the Huamao and Xinpi dikes and remitted grain tax on flooded wasteland—the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 辰州關木稅為利藪，時議移關常德，葉滋恐累民，拒之，請仍舊制。

translations.literal: The Chenzhou Pass timber tax was a source of profit; some proposed moving the pass to Changde; Yezi feared burdening the people, refused, and requested the old system remain.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenzhou Pass timber tax was a lucrative source; some proposed moving the pass to Changde; Yezi feared burdening the people, refused, and urged keeping the old arrangement.

sentences.zh: 行法不避豪貴，興學造士，薦舉優行諸生陳悌為武平知縣，貴金馬為上蔡知縣，劉樵為清平知縣，並為良吏。

translations.literal: He enforced law without avoiding the powerful; promoted learning and cultivated scholars; recommended exemplary students Chen Ti as magistrate of Wuping, Gui Jinma as magistrate of Shangcai, and Liu Qiao as magistrate of Qingping—all became good officials.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the law without fear of the powerful, promoted learning, and recommended exemplary students Chen Ti for Wuping, Gui Jinma for Shangcai, and Liu Qiao for Qingping—all proved capable magistrates.

sentences.zh: 署岳州、辰州二府，攝岳常道副使。

translations.literal: He acted as prefect of Yuezhou and Chenzhou and held the Yuechang Circuit vice commissioner post.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting prefect of Yuezhou and Chenzhou and held the Yuechang Circuit vice commissioner post.

sentences.zh: 久之，授辰沅靖道副使。

translations.literal: After long service he was appointed Chenyuanjing Circuit vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he was appointed Chenyuanjing Circuit vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時苗疆初闢，清林箐，增汛堠，規模肅然。

translations.literal: The Miao frontier had just been opened; he cleared forested ravines, increased guard posts, and established an orderly system.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao frontier had only recently been opened; he cleared forested ravines, increased guard posts, and established an orderly system.

sentences.zh: 所屬綏寧、城步與黔疆犬牙錯。

translations.literal: Suining and Chengbu under his jurisdiction interlocked with the Guizhou frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Suining and Chengbu under his jurisdiction bordered Guizhou in a tangled checkerboard of territories.

sentences.zh: 嘗率數騎，持酒肉鹽菸，循行苗砦。

translations.literal: He once led a few horsemen, carrying wine, meat, salt, and tobacco, touring Miao stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He once led a few horsemen with wine, meat, salt, and tobacco on a tour of Miao stockades.

sentences.zh: 群苗迎拜，謂「上官親我」。

translations.literal: The Miao groups came out to welcome and bow, saying "The superior official treats us as kin."
translations.idiomatic: The Miao came out to welcome him, saying, "Our superior treats us like family."

sentences.zh: 召諸頭人集校場，賜花紅銀牌，宣上德意，勸以禮義。

translations.literal: He summoned all headmen to the drill ground, bestowed floral brocade and silver plaques, proclaimed the emperor's benevolent intent, and exhorted them in ritual and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the headmen to the drill ground, bestowed brocade and silver plaques, proclaimed the emperor's benevolence, and exhorted them in ritual and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 因偕總兵閱兵耀軍容，群苗帖服。

translations.literal: Then together with the regional commander he reviewed troops to display military might, and all Miao groups submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Then with the regional commander he reviewed the troops to display military might, and the Miao submitted.

sentences.zh: 署按察使，調糧儲道，舊有漕費，悉歸公用。

translations.literal: He acted as surveillance commissioner and was transferred to the grain storage circuit; former transport fees all went to public use.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting surveillance commissioner and was transferred to the grain storage circuit; former transport fees were all directed to public use.

sentences.zh: 值貴州苗亂，師進剿，葉滋駐辰州治軍需，剋期辦。

translations.literal: When the Guizhou Miao rebelled, troops advanced to suppress them; Yezi stationed at Chenzhou to manage military supplies and met every deadline.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guizhou Miao rebelled and troops marched to suppress them, Yezi remained at Chenzhou managing military logistics and met every deadline.

sentences.zh: 綏寧苗蠢動，為貴州苗應。

translations.literal: The Suining Miao stirred restlessly, responding to the Guizhou Miao.
translations.idiomatic: The Suining Miao stirred in response to the Guizhou uprising.

sentences.zh: 葉滋條上剿撫事，悉中窾要。

translations.literal: Yezi submitted detailed points on suppression and pacification, all hitting the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Yezi submitted a detailed memorial on suppression and pacification that hit every essential point.

sentences.zh: 大吏令駐綏寧指揮，積勞疾作，卒於山中。

translations.literal: Higher officials ordered him to station at Suining to command; accumulated exertion brought on illness, and he died in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials ordered him to take command at Suining; worn out by accumulated labor, he fell ill and died in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 葉滋初以文學受知，及官於外，所至有聲績。

translations.literal: Yezi was first known through literary learning; in external office wherever he went he gained reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yezi first won notice through his literary accomplishments; in every post he held abroad he earned renown for solid achievement.

sentences.zh: 卒時年僅五十五，世咸惜之。

translations.literal: He died at only fifty-five; the world all regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He died at only fifty-five, and all who knew of him mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 劉而位，字爾爵，山西汾陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Erwei, courtesy name Erjue, was a native of Fenyang in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Erwei, styled Erjue, came from Fenyang in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年舉人，授河南安陽知縣。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the fifty-second year of Kangxi; appointed magistrate of Anyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate in the fifty-second year of Kangxi, he was appointed magistrate of Anyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 有兄弟爭產構訟十餘年者，為據理剖解，至淚下，皆叩頭求罷，案牘遂稀。

translations.literal: Brothers disputing inheritance had brought suit for more than ten years; he judged by reason until they wept, all kowtowed begging to withdraw, and documents became rare.
translations.idiomatic: Two brothers had sued over an inheritance for more than ten years; he judged the case on its merits until both wept, kowtowed, and begged to withdraw—and litigation in his yamen grew scarce.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，遷福建泉州知府，再遷興泉道參議。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng era he was transferred to be prefect of Quanzhou in Fujian, then promoted to Xingquan Circuit administrative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng he was transferred to prefect of Quanzhou in Fujian, then to administrative commissioner of the Xingquan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 鹽政窳敝，商居奇索高直，民苦淡食，不獲已，增價以市。

translations.literal: Salt administration was corrupt and decayed; merchants hoarded and demanded high prices; the people suffered bland diet and, having no choice, paid more to buy.
translations.idiomatic: Salt administration had grown corrupt; merchants hoarded salt and demanded exorbitant prices, and the people, unable to obtain enough, were forced to pay more.

sentences.zh: 既而鹽不足，民惡其壟斷，聚而毆之。

translations.literal: Then salt grew insufficient; the people hated the monopoly and gathered to beat the merchants.
translations.idiomatic: When salt then ran short, the people, resenting the monopoly, gathered to beat the merchants.

sentences.zh: 海舶私梟動逾千百，往捕則持械拒，大獄迭興，羅織牽連，數歲不息。

translations.literal: Private smugglers on seagoing vessels often exceeded a thousand; when pursued they resisted with weapons; major cases arose in succession with entangled implicated parties, continuing for years without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Private smugglers on seagoing vessels often numbered more than a thousand; when pursued they resisted with arms; major cases arose one after another with sprawling indictments, and the turmoil continued for years.

sentences.zh: 而位創議裁引革商，歲額課稅歸灶完納，如農完賦，任人轉運，聽其所之，則諸弊可革而國賦不乏。

translations.literal: Erwei pioneered abolishing licenses and merchant contractors; annual tax quotas would be paid in full at the salterns, like farmers paying land tax; anyone could transport and go where they wished—then all abuses could be reformed without state revenue lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Erwei proposed abolishing transport licenses and licensed merchants, having annual tax quotas paid directly at the salterns as farmers paid land tax, with free transport wherever one chose—thus eliminating abuses while state revenue would not suffer.

sentences.zh: 巡撫趙國麟心韙之，格於例不行。

translations.literal: Governor Zhao Guolin approved in his heart, but regulations blocked implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhao Guolin approved in principle, but existing regulations prevented implementation.

sentences.zh: 未幾，引疾歸。

translations.literal: Before long he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he cited illness and retired home.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，起官四川鹽茶道副使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was recalled to office as Sichuan Salt and Tea Circuit vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianlong he was recalled as Sichuan Salt and Tea Circuit vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蜀鹽產於井，課由井納，民便之。

translations.literal: Shu salt was produced from wells; tax was paid at the wells, convenient for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan salt came from brine wells, with tax paid at the wells—a system convenient for the people.

sentences.zh: 雍正中有請設引招商增課者，四川鹽政自此壞。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng some proposed establishing transport licenses and recruiting merchants to increase tax; Sichuan salt administration was ruined from then on.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng some proposed establishing transport licenses and recruiting merchant contractors to increase revenue—and Sichuan salt administration was ruined from that point on.

sentences.zh: 商無餘貲，運不足額，民持錢不得鹽，而井鹽滯積不售，因以致訌。

translations.literal: Merchants had no surplus capital, transport fell short of quotas, people with money could not obtain salt, well salt stagnated unsold, and riots resulted.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants lacked capital, deliveries fell short of quotas, people with money could not obtain salt, well salt piled up unsold, and disturbances broke out.

sentences.zh: 而位欲事釐剔，​​大吏畏難不可，力爭，愈嫉之。

translations.literal: Erwei wished to undertake reform and elimination of abuses; higher officials feared the difficulty and refused; he argued fiercely, and they hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Erwei wished to undertake thorough reform, but senior officials, fearing the difficulty, refused; he argued fiercely, and they resented him all the more.

sentences.zh: 改松茂道，調永寧道參議。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Songmao Circuit, then to Yongning Circuit administrative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Songmao Circuit, then to administrative commissioner of the Yongning Circuit.

sentences.zh: 居常鬱鬱，不得行其志，惟與諸生講學。

translations.literal: He was usually depressed, unable to carry out his aims, and only lectured students.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in chronic frustration, unable to carry out his aims, and devoted himself to lecturing students.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於官。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office.

sentences.zh: 而位生平服膺王守仁，曰：「尊所聞，行所知，須不流於弊。

translations.literal: Erwei throughout life adhered to Wang Shouren, saying: "Honor what you hear, practice what you know—you must not flow into abuse."
translations.idiomatic: Erwei devoted himself to Wang Shouren, saying: "Honor what you have learned and practice what you know—you must not sink into its abuses."

sentences.zh: 尊陽明而不知其流弊，非善學陽明；

translations.literal: To honor Yangming without knowing its abuses is not good learning of Yangming;
translations.idiomatic: To honor Yangming without understanding its abuses is not to learn Yangming well;

sentences.zh: 尊硃子而不知其流弊，亦非善學硃子。

translations.literal: to honor Master Zhu without knowing its abuses is also not good learning of Master Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: to honor Master Zhu without understanding its abuses is likewise not to learn Zhu well.

sentences.zh: 」蓋謂王氏高明，弊在躐等；

translations.literal: He meant that Wang's school was lofty, its abuse in skipping grades;
translations.idiomatic: He meant that Wang's teaching was sublime, but its abuse lay in skipping steps;

sentences.zh: 硃子格物，弊恐拘而不化。

translations.literal: Zhu's investigation of things—its abuse he feared was rigidity without transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu's investigation of things—he feared its abuse was rigidity without true transformation.

sentences.zh: 著省克引、劉氏家訓，為學者所稱。

translations.literal: He wrote Reflections on Self-Examination and the Liu Family Instructions, praised by scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Reflections on Self-Examination and the Liu Family Instructions, both praised by scholars.

sentences.zh: 論曰：起元深於經術，當朝政尚嚴，能持以平恕。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Qiyuan was deep in classical learning; when court policy favored severity, he could maintain fairness and leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Qiyuan was steeped in the classics; when court policy favored severity, he could still hold to fairness and leniency.

sentences.zh: 師儉以勤敏，繼祖以明肅，並見重於時。

translations.literal: Shijian for diligence and quickness, Jizu for clarity and severity—both were valued in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Shijian for diligence and alertness, Jizu for clarity and severity—both were highly regarded in their day.

sentences.zh: 維翰有幹局，甸尤能澤以儒效。

translations.literal: Weihan had capacity for great affairs; Dian especially could enrich with Confucian effect.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan had a talent for large undertakings; Dian above all could enrich governance with Confucian example.

sentences.zh: 葉滋撫循苗疆，未竟其用。

translations.literal: Yezi pacified the Miao frontier but did not complete his usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Yezi won over the Miao frontier but died before his full potential was realized.

sentences.zh: 而位議變鹽法，亦不得申其志，而但以學術名。

translations.literal: Erwei proposed changing the salt law but also could not express his aims, and was known only by scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: Erwei proposed reforming the salt law but likewise could not carry out his aims, and was known chiefly for his scholarship.

sentences.zh: 國家重視監司，所以擴循良之績，儲封疆之選，若諸人者，可謂無忝矣。

translations.literal: The state values circuit intendants to extend the achievements of good officials and store selections for frontier posts; men such as these can be said not to disgrace the role.
translations.idiomatic: The state values circuit intendants to extend the achievements of worthy officials and prepare selections for frontier posts; men such as these may truly be said not to have disgraced their offices.
